mainEntity.name: How are heating and air conditioning handled in a detached guest cottage?

acceptedAnswer.text: HVAC options for a guest cottage depend on layout, ceiling height, and whether you prefer individual room temperature control. Ductless mini-split heat pumps are the most popular and efficient solution for detached cottages because they avoid bulky ductwork and do not overload the primary residence's air system. Each living zone or bedroom can have its own wall-mounted air handler operated by an independent thermostat. For larger, multi-room cottages with traditional attic spaces, a compact ducted central system can be installed. Proper insulation, quality drywall installation, and energy-efficient windows are critical to keeping cooling loads manageable during humid Florida summers.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ductless mini-split systems are typically used because they provide independent, energy-efficient cooling and heating without requiring ductwork connected to your main home.
